tob-12908: Helena Blavatsky wrote The Key to Theosophy for the curious newcomer, laying out her movement’s beliefs — karma, reincarnation, the brotherhood of humanity — in a simple question-and-answer form. It strips away the dense symbolism of her larger works and speaks plainly. Anyone wondering what Theosophy actually teaches should start here.
tob-13508: Pliny the Younger’s letters are ancient Rome’s most charming correspondence — notes to friends, legal advice, gossip about emperors, and the famous eyewitness account of Vesuvius erupting over Pompeii. Written by a senator who survived Domitian’s terror, they paint daily life in the empire at its height. This first volume opens his celebrated collection.
tob-14508: The Buddha’s most beloved set of sayings, here in Max Müller’s classic rendering. Chapter by chapter, these short verses urge the reader to master anger, speak truthfully, and walk the path of clear sight. Few holy texts say so much in so few words — which is why the Dhammapada has been turned into English more than almost any other Buddhist work.
tob-4108: James Legge’s Chinese Classics is the great English door to Confucian writ — Analects, Great Learning, Mean, and Mencius, with text, rendering, and notes. His life’s labor in Hong Kong and Oxford set the bar for the field. The volumes stay the bedrock of English study of China.
tob-10008: Virgil’s Æneid is Rome’s great folk-epic — Aeneas fleeing fallen Troy, his doomed love for Dido, his fated founding of a new Troy in Italy. Conington’s plain-prose rendering keeps its majesty. The poem bent Europe’s letters for two thousand years.
tob-13808: Bell’s Hafiz in a third Englishing — the Shiraz master’s wine-songs of nightingales and the Fair One, in English verse. Wrought when she was deep in Persian lore, her versions bear the tune of the original. Hafiz stays the poet no Persian shelf is whole without.
tob-0108: A second Englishing of Basil Valentine’s Twelve Keys — the twelve emblem plates shewing the Great Work’s steps, from burning-down to the stone’s crowning. Verse and discourse veil the privities in parable. The book ranks among gold-lore’s most treasured texts.
tob-4008: Giordano Bruno’s 1584 talk-book holds the All unbounded, with worlds past counting — a sight that helped fetch him to the stake in 1600. His world-frame leapt past Copernicus to a shoreless cosmos. The book is a martyring of the mind’s eye.
tob-4208: This 1897 Yoga Sastra sifts Patanjali’s Sutras — the ground-text of yoga thought — with searching care. The work unfolds the rede of gathered mind, deep brooding, and freeing. It bore ordered yoga-thinking to English readers. A landmark of early yoga book-lore.
tob-9108: Vitruvius’s Ten Books — in Gwilt’s Englishing — are the one Roman builder’s writ to live on, on fanes, waterworks, engines, and town-laying. The work steered builders from the Renaissance on. Palladio, Wren, and Jefferson learned their orders from him. It stays the bible of classic building.
cia-0000119208: An October 1984 report identifying a possible American POW camp in Saravane province, Laos. A decade after the war, leads like this one still had to be chased — satellite photos, defector tips, and hope. The entry shows the POW/MIA hunt grinding on, long after the helicopters left.
cia-0000119708: A November 1953 estimate of probable developments in Brazil. Getulio Vargas was back in power, steering a nationalist course between the superpowers. The document forecasts a giant whose future would swing between democracy and dictatorship for decades.
cia-0000124308: An April 1951 report on American prisoners of war in Canton, China. Korean War airmen and others vanished into the Chinese prison system, and every sighting was reported. The entry is one fragment of the long, painful effort to account for POWs the enemy would not acknowledge.
cia-0000132208: Situation Report 525 with an oil update: the slick keeps moving — Saddam's deliberate spill spreading through the Gulf. The environmental weapon was as shocking as any bomb. The document tracks the black tide: war's damage, measured in barrels and beaches.
cia-0000132308: Situation Report 618: Saddam reportedly considering seeking asylum — the truncated title cuts off where. Rumors of the dictator's flight swirled as his armies collapsed. The entry is the ultimate wartime rumor: the tyrant, packing his bags.
cia-0000132608: Item 2 in the July 1960 series: Colombia's position on the Cuban issue. Bogota was staking out its stance in the continental debate. The document is the position: the republic, declaring.
cia-0000135908: A 1954 assessment of the present status and possible future course of PBSUCCESS. The operation, evaluated mid-stream. The document is the review: the status, judged — the future, projected.
cia-0000136208: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on refugees leaving WSBURNT. The human tide, noted. The document is the flight: the refugees, counted.
cia-0000136308: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CADICK with guidance on the ALPHA and BETA plans — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The alternative plans, explained. The document is the guidance: the plans, briefed.
cia-0000136908: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on sabotage possibilities. The options, weighed. The document is the possibilities: the sabotage, considered.
un-sc-res-108: Security Council Resolution 108, adopted in 1955. The mid-fifties Council. The number and year are preserved; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1808: Security Council Resolution 1808, adopted in April 2008 — the Georgia resolution, extending the UN observer mission in the Abkhaz conflict zone. Months before the Russo-Georgian war, the watch continued. The resolution is the extension: the observers, kept.
un-sc-res-2008: Security Council Resolution 2008, cataloged with the year 2012 — the numbering suggests 2011, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
cia-0000132508: A 1961 CIA Cuba file — number 0000132508. The invasion year's paperwork. The document is the record: the island, filed.
cia-0000135608: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135608. The invasion year — the brigade's words, kept. The document is the year: the papers, fateful.
cia-0000135708: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135708. The exiles' papers, held by the agency. The entry is the holding: the papers, secured.
plos-pone-0000008: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on molecular adaptation during adaptive radiation in a Hawaiian endemic — the truncated title cuts off the organism. Island evolution, written in DNA. The paper is the radiation: the genes, adapting.
cia-0000137108: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000137108. The training year's papers. The document is the training: the brigade, preparing.
cia-0000137308: A 1960 CIA briefing for the National Security Council on Cuba — number 0000137308. The series of briefings continued. The document is the series: the briefings, many.
alexander-locke-1908: Samuel Alexander's Locke, published in 1908 — a short critical study of John Locke, the empiricist philosopher of toleration and government by consent. Alexander, himself a major philosopher, reads his predecessor with a practitioner's eye. The book is the study: the empiricist, examined.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d108: A memorandum by the first secretary of the embassy in the Soviet Union, Bohlen — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 108. The Moscow embassy's thinking, on paper. The memo is the thinking: Bohlen, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d208: The Secretary of War Stimson to the president's special assistant Hopkins — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 208. The War Department wrote the insider. The memo is the insider's: Stimson, to Hopkins.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d308: A revised American draft of the communiqué — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 308. The second version. The draft is the revision: the words, refined.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d408: Communiqué: First Draft — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 408. The announcement's first version. The draft is the first: the words, attempted.
arxiv-2605-08808: Describing a 3D scene in words demands knowing how surfaces bend and connect, not just which pixels sit where. Ziyao He and coauthors propose curvature-aware captioning, with geodesic attention that follows the surface geometry to guide the description. The 2026 paper brings ideas from differential geometry into the image-captioning pipeline.
arxiv-2605-08908: Hardware accelerators live or die by their caches: keep the right data close and deadlines get met. Ayushi Agarwal, Anannya Mathur, and Preeti Ranjan Panda present HyDRA, which decides what is cacheable based on deadlines and data reuse. The 2026 paper is computer-architecture research for real-time accelerators.
arxiv-2605-09408: Predicting missing links in directed graphs with rich node attributes is big business — fraud detection, recommendations, biology. Riccardo Porcedda, Francesca Chiaromonte, Fabrizio Lillo, and colleagues bring gravity-inspired GraphSAGE to the task. The 2026 paper is graph learning with physical intuition about attraction.
arxiv-2605-09608: Continual post-training teaches models new skills while erasing old ones — a geometry conflict playing out in weight space. Yuanyi Wang, Yifan Yang, Su Lu, and colleagues explain the conflict and learn to control the forgetting. The 2026 paper maps exactly where new knowledge collides with old.
arxiv-2605-09808: Building genuinely collaborative LLM assistants needs user simulators — but how useful are those simulators, really? Joseph Suh, Ayush Raj, Minwoo Kang, and Serina Chang quantify the utility rigorously and carefully. The 2026 paper carefully measures the measurers of human-AI collaboration today.
arxiv-2605-10108: Named entity recognition and relation extraction, performed jointly in one unified framework — GLiNER-Relex. Ihor Stepanov, Oleksandr Lukashov, Mykhailo Shtopko, and colleagues build it. The 2026 paper is information extraction unified. It finds entities and their relations together, jointly.
plos-pone-0003408: Geneticists caught a gene being controlled from far away in this 2008 paper. The peptidylarginine deiminase enzymes, which modify proteins by converting arginine to citrulline, are regulated by a distant DNA enhancer that loops the chromosome to reach them. That looping lets the AP-1 switch flip these genes on, a vivid example of long-range control in the human genome.
plos-pone-0003508: Biochemists found turmeric's active ingredient jamming a sugar-detox enzyme in this 2008 paper. Curcumin inhibited glyoxalase 1, which normally neutralizes the reactive byproduct methylglyoxal, offering a possible molecular link to curcumin's reported anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor effects. The result gives the spice compound a concrete biochemical target to investigate.
plos-pone-0003608: Epidemiologists mapped the viral landscape among injectors in Liuzhou, China, in this 2008 study. Hepatitis C alone and combined with HIV are growing problems among injection drug users, so the team charted prevalence and genotypes of both infections. The molecular map guides targeted prevention where the twin epidemics overlap.
plos-pone-0003708: In 2008, Rogers and Gore compared the noise in brain-connectivity studies. Functional MRI can map which brain regions fire together, but different analysis choices pull in different sources of variation. Their head-to-head comparison tells imagers which methods give the steadiest read on brain networks.
plos-pone-0003808: Bishop, Pai, and Schmitt measured the sneak in cats' steps in this 2008 paper. Their whole-body mechanics analysis of stealthy walking revealed how cats keep locomotion cheap and quiet. The energy budget of a prowl turns out to be a masterclass in efficient movement.
plos-pone-0003908: In 2008, a team tested whether a PET scan tracer could spot lung cancer treatment working early. The tracer, called FLT, lights up dividing cells, and the team imaged non-small cell lung cancer patients starting erlotinib. Tumors that would respond dimmed on the scan days before they shrank. The early read could spare patients weeks on a drug that will not help them.
plos-pone-0004008: In 2008, Vukojevic, Ming, and D'Addario watched alcohol and its blocker meet. Using live-cell microscopy, they studied ethanol and naltrexone at the mu-opioid receptor. The single-molecule tracking revealed how the two rival drugs share the receptor. The nanoscale view will inform better future treatment strategies against alcohol dependence.
plos-pone-0004108: In 2009, Hashimoto, Qu, and Ahsan read gene starts at massive scale. Their high-resolution survey of the 5-prime-end transcriptome used a next-generation DNA sequencer. Tag-based sequencing captured millions of gene-start snapshots. The new catalog sharpens maps of where genes truly begin.
plos-pone-0004208: In 2009, Joshi, Ganesan, and Cheney mapped a killer-signal circuit. The PtdIns 3-kinase/Akt pathway steered macrophage killing of antibody-coated lymphoma cells. Blocking the pathway blunted the attack. The circuit guides antibody-therapy design. The finding sharpens the science behind antibody drugs.
plos-pone-0004308: In 2009, a Thai team tracked deadly staph in the tropics. Staphylococcus aureus blood infections were studied in a Thai tropical hospital. Outcomes and drug resistance patterns were mapped quite fully. The new data fill a tropical knowledge gap at last.
plos-pone-0356108: Peer review decides who gets research money, yet two reviewers often reach opposite verdicts on the same proposal. This paper mines 134,000 reviews from four funding agencies to find out why experts disagree. Pinpointing the sources of the split — from different standards to simple noise — it offers funders concrete ways to make grant decisions fairer and more consistent.
plos-pone-0358008: Brain injury can rob people of social intuition — missing sarcasm, misreading faces. T-ScEmo4ALL Plus+ is a treatment for social cognition disorders in patients with acquired brain injury and neuropsychiatric problems, and this paper tested it in a single-case experimental design. The detailed case results show whether the therapy rebuilds the social brain and how large the gains are.
plos-pone-0357708: Smart homes must parse intent from speech — ‘turn off the kitchen lights’ should just work. This paper constructed and optimized a deep-learning intent classification model for smart home dialogue. The optimized model helps voice assistants understand what residents actually want, making the connected home feel less dumb.
plos-pone-0357908: Corneal transplants restore sight — but only if grieving families consent to donation. This study identified factors affecting family consent at a hospital-based eye bank in a tertiary Israeli medical center. The findings show what moves families toward saying yes in their hardest hour.
plos-pone-0346308: Clinical trials run on data systems — and choosing the wrong one is expensive. This paper published a protocol for a scoping review of data capture, collection, management, and storage systems for clinical research. The planned review will map the crowded landscape so trialists can choose wisely.
plos-pone-0357608: Medical research has an inclusion problem: trials too often exclude the people they aim to help. This paper described developing an inclusive research methods strategy for the Manchester Biomedical Research Centre and Clinical Research Facility. The strategy aims to make studies genuinely reflect the diverse public they serve.
plos-pone-0356808: Smartwatches promise lab-grade fitness numbers — but do they deliver? This study tested the accuracy of VO2 max, heart rate, and energy expenditure measurements from the Google Pixel Watch 3. The validation results tell athletes and coaches exactly what to trust on their wrist — and what to take with salt.
plos-pone-0356608: Community mental health succeeds or fails through human relationships. This paper evaluated staff experiences of relational care in Intensive Community Care Services versus treatment as usual. The comparison reveals what intensive community care actually feels like from the inside — for the workers holding it together.
plos-pone-0357808: The elusive MB2 canal in upper molars is the root canal treatment’s most common trap. This CBCT study applied machine learning to predict the canal’s presence in permanent maxillary first and second molars. The AI helps dentists find the hidden canal before it causes a failed root canal.
plos-pone-0357408: Children in Malawi face steep, specific barriers to HIV services — and generic programs miss them. This multifaceted research protocol will investigate strategies to enhance children’s access to HIV services in the country. The planned study centers children’s actual needs rather than adult assumptions about them.
plos-pone-0356908: Aphasia assessment in Urdu was missing a validated quick tool — until now. This paper adapted the Quick Aphasia Battery into Urdu and established its psychometric properties. The adaptation brings reliable language assessment to hundreds of millions of Urdu speakers.
plos-pone-0357108: How do humans estimate magnitudes — and can we measure the process cleanly? This paper validated the magnitude Stroop task, in which irrelevant magnitude information interferes with judgments. The validated task gives cognitive researchers a precise tool for probing number sense.
plos-pone-0357008: A mother’s social media habits can reach all the way to her children’s teeth. This study of immigrant families linked social media addiction, maternal mental health, and children’s oral health behaviors. The chain of effects reveals a hidden pathway of harm — and a place to intervene.
plos-pone-0356508: Cancer patients depend on pharmacists getting antimicrobial prophylaxis exactly right. This paper developed and psychometrically evaluated an assessment tool for pharmacists’ knowledge and practice on the topic. The validated tool identifies knowledge gaps before they become patient harm.
plos-pone-0355408: Childhood stunting in Nigeria isn’t just about poverty — it’s about intersecting disadvantages. This intersectional analysis examined early childhood stunting across Nigerian households. The layered findings show how gender, wealth, education, and region combine to stunt children’s growth.
plos-pone-0345608: Ethiopian children with cancer were invisible in national data — until now. This paper described implementing a National Pediatric Cancer Registry using a systems ‘A3’ thinking approach. The registry gives the country its first real picture of childhood cancer — the foundation for every improvement to follow.
plos-pone-0352608: Prestressed concrete piles lose their prestress over time — threatening structural safety. This paper studied prestress loss and safety performance of retard-bonded prestressed cast-in-place piles. The engineering analysis ensures these foundational elements keep holding up the structures above them.
plos-pone-0356008: Gut microbes produce metabolites that talk to the immune system — with implications for liver disease. This integrative bioinformatics analysis identified gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated immune targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis. The findings nominate the gut-liver axis as a therapeutic frontier.
plos-pone-0355508: Proteus mirabilis — a urinary pathogen — is turning multidrug-resistant in Ethiopian hospitals. This genomic epidemiology study tracked resistant and ESBL-producing strains in a military referral hospital. The genomic surveillance exposes transmission patterns that infection control must break.
plos-pone-0355608: Infection strikes cardiorenal syndrome patients — when heart and kidneys fail together — with devastating effect. This paper examined infection’s impact on decongestion and kidney outcomes in type 1 cardiorenal syndrome. The findings guide clinicians managing the dangerous triad of heart failure, kidney injury, and infection.
plos-pone-0353308: In South Korea’s family-centered culture, caregivers’ voices shape chronic illness decisions — but are they heard? This qualitative study asked whose voice counts in shared decision-making for chronic illness. The findings reveal the invisible labor of family caregivers — and the recognition they’re denied.
europmc-pmc2834608: DNA-based breeding predictions work best when every animal is genotyped, but that is expensive. This 2010 paper tackles genomic prediction when some animals lack genotypes. The authors develop methods that blend genotyped and ungenotyped relatives. Their approach made genomic selection practical for real herds with patchy data.
europmc-pmc2873308: Death certificates are messy, and this 2010 paper brings math to clean them. The authors build algorithms for enhancing the public health use of national causes-of-death data. Their methods fix misclassified deaths. The work underpins global burden-of-disease estimates.
europmc-pmc2880408: Tiny RNAs tie to many diseases, and this 2010 paper ranks them. The authors prioritize disease microRNAs through a network linking the human phenome to the microRNAome. Their method spots the most promising candidates. The work guided follow-up on RNA-based disease clues.
europmc-pmc2928208: Counting gene reads needs sound stats. This 2010 paper introduces baySeq, a Bayesian method for spotting genes that truly differ between samples. The authors' math handles the noise in count data. Their tool became an RNA-seq staple in labs. It is still cited by sequencing studies today.
europmc-pmc2947508: Public gene data holds buried treasure for meta-analysis. This 2010 paper offers ontology-based meta-analysis of global high-throughput public data collections. The authors' method unifies scattered studies with shared terms. Their tool mines the data deluge. Researchers reuse it to squeeze more from old datasets.
europmc-pmc2970908: Damaged power plants get hauled to the cell's center for disposal. This 2010 paper shows p62 teams with Parkin to cluster depolarized mitochondria near the nucleus. The authors reveal the hauling crew. Their work details Parkinson's-linked cleanup. Broken cleanup lets toxic junk pile up.
europmc-pmc3026008: A cell-cycle gene drives growth through a master switch. This 2011 paper shows E2F1 steers cell growth via mTORC1 signals. The authors link the two pathways. Their work clarifies growth control. Cancer hijacks this growth wiring. mTOR blockers already treat some tumors.
europmc-pmc3040208: Drug-factory rivers breed superbugs. This 2011 paper finds Indian river mud laced with antibiotics breeds drug-proof germs. The authors' gene survey sounds the alarm. Their work spurred regulation. Resistance genes hop between germ species there. The world took notice of pharma pollution.
europmc-pmc3040608: Heat waves kill, and this 2011 paper counts the toll. The authors track death risk across 43 US cities during heat waves. Their data reveals who dies first. The work guides heat policy. The elderly and poor bear the brunt. Cooling centers save lives, the authors urge.
europmc-pmc3071808: MRSA clones got a field guide. This 2011 paper maps the world's pandemic, epidemic, and sporadic MRSA strains. The authors chart each lineage's turf. Their guide aids outbreak response. Hospitals ID the culprit strain faster. The guide is free for infection teams.
europmc-pmc6512308: Immunotherapy works wonders for some lung cancers and fails for others, so doctors need a way to predict who benefits. This study tested tumor mutational burden measured from a blood draw - counting cancer mutations floating in the bloodstream - in non-small cell lung cancer patients. Higher blood-based scores lined up with better responses, suggesting a simple blood test could guide treatment choices.
europmc-pmc6513508: Retinal vein occlusion - a blockage in the eye's blood vessels - is the second most common retinal vascular disorder, striking an estimated 16.4 million people worldwide in 2008. This systematic review and meta-analysis gathers a decade of new data to update who gets it, how often, and why. The numbers give eye doctors and health planners a fresh picture of a leading cause of vision loss.
europmc-pmc6583308: Reading chest X-rays for serious disease is skilled, tiring work - and misses happen. A deep-learning system trained on thousands of radiographs learned to flag major thoracic diseases automatically. Tested against expert readers, the algorithm held its own, promising faster triage and a safety net for busy clinics.
europmc-pmc6647108: More older Britons than ever need help with daily life - and the system strains to provide it. This scoping review maps unmet care and support needs among older people, sorted through a WHO framework. The categorization gives policymakers a clearer picture of where help falls short.
europmc-pmc6707308: More microbial species usually means a healthier ecosystem - but which differences matter? This study shows that variation between local bacterial communities (beta-diversity) steers assembly in predictable, deterministic ways, constraining what the community can do. Diversity's hidden structure, not just its headcount, shapes function.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-808: The pension backstop needed better bosses in 2007 — GAO's report says the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation's governance needed repairs. The findings target the leadership of the insurer of last resort for retirements. The report warns that the safety net's own safety needed attention.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-708: Modernizing the FHA was a budget riddle in 2007 — GAO's report says the reform ideas carried real program and dollar consequences for taxpayers. The findings price the proposals in plain terms. The report warns Congress to read the fine print before rebuilding the housing agency.
gao-gaoreports-b-299408: Dellew Corporation took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest against bid law. Every protest gets the same careful reading, whatever the trade.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-408: The VA's hospital-building choices needed a scorecard in 2007, and GAO's report says the department should track how its asset decisions played out. The findings demand real follow-through on the plans. The report's point is firm: the blueprint is a promise, not a result.
gao-gaoreports-b-299108: SEI Group took its February 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Short names get the same long, careful hearing.
openalex-w7206191808: Medical residency programs in Brazil are moving toward curricula built around real competencies rather than isolated subjects. This study looks at three multiprofessional Family Health residency programs whose teaching plans use integrated, competency-based designs with active learning methods. The authors gather the perceptions of tutors working inside these programs. It offers an inside view of how competency-based training feels to the people delivering it.
openalex-w7204550808: A child's start in life still depends heavily on the family's wallet. This systematic review studies how social inequality shapes child development across social classes. The authors synthesize research on the gaps in health, learning, and opportunity. A evidence-driven look at how unfair the starting line is, and what it costs children.
openalex-w7204201608: Wet macular degeneration steals central vision, but regular eye injections can hold it back. This paper reviews periodic intravitreal injections of VEGF blockers: how they stop abnormal blood vessels in the retina. The authors cover the treatment that changed elder eye care. A clinical review of medicine buying back sight, one shot at a time.
pmc-13456108: This 2026 plant pathology paper identifies AaVCX, a vacuolar calcium/proton exchanger in a pathogenic fungus, as a regulator of calcium balance, the formation of infection structures, and overall virulence. Disrupting how the fungus manages calcium cripples its attack on plants. The exchanger emerges as a candidate target for crop protection.
pmc-13456708: In this 2026 dermatology study, researchers compared nail changes — seen clinically and under dermoscopy, a magnified skin-surface exam — across rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, and psoriasis. The prospective comparison maps which nail signs belong to which disease. Nails are easy to examine, so reliable patterns could speed diagnosis.
pmc-13445608: This 2026 pilot study tested a wireless, wearable ultrasound patch for estimating blood volume loss — critical in trauma and surgery where every minute counts. The device aims to replace invasive monitoring with a stick-on sensor. The pilot results suggest the concept works and deserves larger trials.
pmc-13489708: This 2026 machine learning paper studies TCR–peptide binding prediction — forecasting which immune receptors recognize which protein fragments — and shows that when multimodal fusion fails, contrastive alignment stabilizes the model. The finding is a practical lesson for AI in immunology: how you combine data types decides whether the model works.
pmc-13439208: In this 2026 study, adolescents with ADHD underwent aerobic exercise while researchers measured motor inhibition and cortical excitability — how the brain brakes movement and how excitable its circuits are. Exercise had both immediate and lasting effects. The findings support exercise as a real, measurable intervention for ADHD.
pmc-13433008: This 2026 soil ecology paper showed that soil texture and neonicotinoid pesticide exposure together shape bacterial communities and their functions in farmland, with effects that play out over prolonged exposure. Pesticides don't act in a vacuum — the soil itself modulates the damage. The findings inform more realistic risk assessment.
pmc-13428608: This 2026 cancer paper shows that SOCS3 — suppressor of cytokine signaling 3 — regulates glioma stem cell maintenance and the immune microenvironment through the STAT signaling pathway. Brain tumor stem cells drive recurrence, and SOCS3 sits at a control point. The mechanism offers a new therapeutic angle for glioblastoma.
pmc-13557008: In this 2026 heart failure paper — a prespecified subanalysis of the FRESH-UP study — researchers tested whether changing fluid-intake advice affects outcomes in chronic heart failure. Fluid restriction is traditional but poorly evidenced. The subanalysis puts the advice to a rigorous test.
pmc-13471808: This 2026 paper described ENHANCE, a global collaborative research program investigating homeopathy's role in antimicrobial stewardship. The premise is controversial. The program description lays out the research agenda.
pmc-13468808: This 2026 cardiology paper traced the spectrum of pregnancy-induced cardiac remodeling — from healthy adaptive hypertrophy to peripartum cardiomyopathy. Pregnancy stresses the heart along a continuum. The spectrum reframes the disease.
pmc-13464908: This 2026 surgical paper addressed pulmonary metastasectomy after liver transplantation — indications, timing, and decision-making across tumor types. Operating on transplant recipients is high-stakes. The paper guides the decisions.
pmc-13429108: In this 2026 obstetrics paper, CPT1A, CYGB, and MRPL3 emerged as pre-eclampsia biomarkers from oxidative stress-related gene analysis. The dangerous pregnancy complication needs early markers. The genes are candidates.
pmc-13422908: This 2026 paper described human-centered design of a multistakeholder reporting dashboard for disseminating HIV implementation research in the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative. Research must reach implementers. The dashboard design is the deliverable.
pmc-13586408: A 2026 study evaluating the Prodromal Questionnaire-16 for screening and predicting psychosis in autistic adults, with cross-sectional and longitudinal findings. The screening tool needed autism-specific validation. The evaluation provides it.
pmc-13571308: A 2026 study of early and long-term mechanical complications after carotid artery stenting. The neck artery procedure's device risks were tracked. The complication data inform consent.
pmc-13525508: A 2026 case series asking whether injectable breast augmentation is the missing history in breast abscess in young nulliparous women. The cosmetic procedure's complication was investigated. The series raises the question.
pmc-13510108: A 2026 green chemistry paper on eco-friendly extraction and valorization of horned melon peel and pulp — optimizing phenolic recovery and evaluating bioactivity (the title is truncated). The waste became a resource. The optimization is the method.
pmc-13501308: A 2026 paper on a linear interpretable model for drug target prediction. The simplicity preserved interpretability. The model is the trade-off.
pmc-13494508: A 2026 stroke paper showing downregulation of Lgals3 (galectin-3) alleviated inflammation and apoptosis in a mouse cerebral ischemia/reperfusion model. The gene's suppression protected the brain. The alleviation is the therapeutic hint.
pmc-13479108: This 2026 correction notice amended a systematic review on biopsy-based immune biomarkers predicting neoadjuvant therapy response in rectal cancer (the title is truncated). Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13467408: In this 2026 urology paper, risk of new-onset postoperative depression after holmium laser enucleation versus TURP for benign prostatic hyperplasia was compared (the title is truncated). The prostate surgeries' mood effects were tested. The comparison is the finding.
pmc-13348508: A 2026 scoping review exploring patients' and professionals' views on psychology provision in primary care (the title is truncated). The primary care psychology's reception was mapped. The review informs service design.
pmc-13426008: This 2026 case report covered airway management and retrieval of a large ingested foreign body. The dramatic extraction was detailed. The case teaches the technique.
pmc-13431008: A 2026 single-center retrospective analysis of the proteinuria selectivity index as a predictor of remission and rituximab efficacy in primary membranous nephropathy (the title is truncated). The index forecasted treatment response. The predicting aids nephrology.
pmc-13543908: This 2026 review assessed the pandemic potential of Nipah virus — from molecular pathogenesis to ecological spillover risks. The deadly virus's threat was evaluated. The assessing is the preparedness input.
pmc-13526308: A 2026 case report of acquired hemophilia A in an elderly patient receiving clopidogrel — drug-induced or age-associated autoimmunity? The question frames the case. The report weighs the evidence.
pmc-13473108: In this 2026 qualitative study, perceptions and protective experiences regarding reproductive hazards were examined among operating room healthcare workers of childbearing age. The workers' concerns were voiced. The perceptions inform occupational health.
pmc-13473008: This 2026 materials paper examined the size effect on mechanical and permeability properties of porous bone structures fabricated by selective laser melting. The 3D-printed bone's properties scaled. The size effect guides implant design.

arxiv-2606-16008: The pressureless Euler system is a set of equations describing how crowds of particles — dust, traffic, or stars — move without any internal pressure pushing them apart. This mathematics paper studies what steady, unchanging states (equilibria) those equations allow in one dimension. It is a pure analysis result aimed at specialists in fluid and kinetic equations.
arxiv-2606-16208: Training robots needs enormous amounts of demonstration data, and choosing the right data matters as much as collecting it. ATHENA speeds up "influence functions" — a technique for measuring each training example's effect — across many tasks and mixed data types, helping curate better robot datasets faster. It targets robotics and machine learning researchers.
arxiv-2606-16308: Bridges and buildings need constant health checks. This paper applies physics-informed sensitivity analysis — combining engineering physics with data-driven methods — to assess structural health, tested on a mixed steel-concrete bridge. The approach pinpoints which measurements matter most for spotting damage, aimed at civil engineers monitoring real infrastructure.
arxiv-2606-16408: Most generative AI handles one direction: text to image, or image to text. MUNI is a unified multimodal latent diffusion model for "any-to-any" generation — any input type to any output type, coherently. The paper presents the architecture for researchers building all-in-one generative models.
arxiv-2606-16708: An economics-style paper on risk versus uncertainty — two words people mix up. Risk means you know the odds; uncertainty means you don't even know the odds. The paper explores that divide and what it means for decisions. Thin evidence: the catalog entry carries only the title.
